description: Parameters needed to the corresponding task specification in eTaSL

from-core_task_lib-version-1.0.2.description:
Library core_task_lib version 1.0.2.
 Set to true to indicate that task specification comes from the library above. 
 Library description: Library with basic task specifications that may be needed in most applications
Authors: Santiago Iregui (KU Leuven), Erwin Aertbeliën (KU Leuven), Federico Ulloa (KU Leuven)

file_path.description: File path of the corresponding task specification

parameters.description: List of parameters needed to define an instance of the task specification

K_relative_rotation.description: Feedback gain [1/s] of the constraint that keeps the relative orientation w.r.t. base_frame (used when activate_angular is true). Larger values correct deviations faster; too large values can cause oscillations or saturate the joint velocities

task_frame.description: Name of the robot frame (as defined in the robot model, e.g. URDF link or tcp_frame) whose pose is kept constant relative to base_frame

activate_angular.description: If true, the orientation of the task frame relative to base_frame is kept at its initial value, i.e. the task frame rotates along with base_frame. If false, the orientation of the task frame is kept fixed w.r.t. the robot base frame

weight_position.description: Weight (dimensionless) of the position constraint (relative or fixed, depending on activate_linear) w.r.t. the other constraints of the same priority. Only relative weights matter: a higher weight makes this constraint dominate when the constraints conflict

K_fixed_position.description: Feedback gain [1/s] of the constraint that keeps the position of the task frame fixed w.r.t. the robot base frame (used when activate_linear is false). Larger values correct deviations faster

K_relative_position.description: Feedback gain [1/s] of the constraint that keeps the relative position w.r.t. base_frame (used when activate_linear is true). Larger values correct deviations faster (more aggressive tracking); too large values can cause oscillations or saturate the joint velocities

base_frame.description: Name of the input channel (Frame) with the pose of the moving base frame, expressed w.r.t. the robot base frame. The task frame keeps its initial pose relative to this frame. It must be provided by an input handler, e.g. a PoseInputHandler or a TFInputHandler

weight_rotation.description: Weight (dimensionless) of the orientation constraint (relative or fixed, depending on activate_angular) w.r.t. the other constraints of the same priority. Only relative weights matter: a higher weight makes this constraint dominate when the constraints conflict

K_fixed_rotation.description: Feedback gain [1/s] of the constraint that keeps the orientation of the task frame fixed w.r.t. the robot base frame (used when activate_angular is false). Larger values correct deviations faster

execution_time.description: Time [s] after which the task stops automatically (exit monitor). If execution_time <= 0 (default 0), the task does not stop by itself and runs until stopped externally

activate_linear.description: If true, the position of the task frame relative to base_frame (expressed in base_frame) is kept at its initial value, i.e. the task frame follows the motion of base_frame. If false, the position of the task frame is kept fixed at its initial value w.r.t. the robot base frame

is-keep_relative_initial_pose.description:
Task Specification: keep_relative_initial_pose.etasl.lua
Set to true to indicate that the task uses the task specification mentioned above. 
 Task description: Keeps the pose of a task frame (a robot frame) relative to a moving base frame equal to the relative pose they had at the start of the task, so that the task frame follows the motion of the base frame (e.g. a tracked object).
Position and orientation are handled separately (activate_linear / activate_angular): when activated, the relative position resp. orientation w.r.t. base_frame is kept at its initial value; when deactivated, the position resp. orientation of the task frame is kept fixed at its initial value w.r.t. the robot base frame (root frame of the robot model), ignoring the motion of base_frame.
Input channel: a Frame named as the parameter base_frame (default "base_frame"), giving the base frame pose w.r.t. the robot base frame, typically provided by a PoseInputHandler or TFInputHandler.
The task runs until stopped externally, unless execution_time > 0, in which case it exits after execution_time seconds. Outputs: time and the position (x_tf, y_tf, z_tf) [m] of the task frame w.r.t. the robot base frame.
